channel.title: DJWEIRDNASTY News
channel.description: Latest national, entertainment, music, and sports news from DJWEIRDNASTY.

item.title: Converse Pulls Advertisement After Backlash Over Imagery
item.description: Converse removed an advertisement featuring aespa singer Karina after online criticism that its imagery evoked Ku Klux Klan symbolism and the history of lynching.

item.title: DJWEIRDNASTY Joins National DJ Meeting Featuring Belly Gang Kushington
item.description: DJWEIRDNASTY took part in a national DJ Zoom meeting with Belly Gang Kushington, DJ Coalition, Nerve DJs and Fleet DJs for a listening session on new singles 'WTF Goin' featuring 21 Savage and 'No Jewelry.'

item.title: Murder Suspect Allegedly Turned Away After Attempting to Surrender at NYPD Precinct
item.description: Tiliek Shamel Thompson, accused in the death of Lovay Williams, allegedly attempted to surrender at an NYPD precinct but was allowed to leave.

item.title: Papoose Fires Back at Remy Ma With New Diss Track 'Jezebel'
item.description: Papoose releases a new diss track titled 'Jezebel' aimed at Remy Ma, addressing their marriage, accusations of infidelity, and claims he wrote some of her rhymes.

item.title: Sexyy Red Faces Potential $5 Million Default Judgment in Lawsuit
item.description: St. Louis rapper Sexyy Red faces a potential $5 million default judgment after allegedly sharing the home address of her child's paternal grandmother online.

item.title: AI Safety Debate Intensifies as Researchers Warn of Potential Extinction Risk
item.description: Researchers with experience at OpenAI and Anthropic warn that increasingly powerful AI systems could pose an existential threat to humanity.

item.title: 25 Years Later, America Reflects on the Lives and Legacy of 9/11
item.description: A quarter-century after the September 11 terrorist attacks, Americans gathered to remember the 2,977 people killed and reflect on an event that permanently altered the country.

item.title: Lil Durk Wins Major Courtroom Victory as Jury Clears Him in Los Angeles Case
item.description: A federal jury found Lil Durk not guilty on all charges in a Los Angeles murder-for-hire prosecution connected to a 2022 shooting.

item.title: Lakeland Infant Death Leads to Arrest After Investigators Link Mother's Ring to Skull Injuries
item.description: Jessica Vlasac, 42, was arrested in Lakeland, Florida after investigators linked her ring to skull injuries on her 3-month-old son.

item.title: Bloodhound Q50 Dead at 22 After Deadly Chicago Shooting
item.description: Chicago rapper Bloodhound Q50, real name Mikquale T. Cooper, was killed early Sunday after gunfire erupted at a gas station in the city's Fuller Park neighborhood.

item.title: Arch Manning Apologizes After Comments About AI Video Depicting Holly Rowe
item.description: Texas quarterback Arch Manning has apologized to ESPN reporter Holly Rowe after his comments about a manipulated AI video depicting Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian appearing to strike her.

item.title: DistroKid Hit With Lawsuit From Universal Music Group Over AI Music and Copyright Claims
item.description: Universal Music Group has sued DistroKid in federal court, alleging copyright infringement, deceptive business practices, and the unauthorized distribution of AI-generated music.

item.title: Eagles Survive Commanders, 24–22, in Thrilling Week 1 Opener
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles opened the 2026 regular season with a dramatic 24–22 victory over the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field.

item.title: Former Titans Scout Blaise Taylor Gets Two Life Sentences in Nashville Murder Case
item.description: Blaise Taylor, a former Tennessee Titans scout, was sentenced to two consecutive life terms plus 22 years for the murders of his girlfriend Jade Benning and their unborn child.

item.title: Carmen Bryan Files Civil Lawsuit Against N.O.R.E. Over Alleged 1999 Incident
item.description: Carmen Bryan has filed a civil lawsuit against rapper N.O.R.E., accusing him of sexually assaulting her at a New York City nightclub in 1999.

item.title: Sixers, Flyers Reveal New Look for Planned South Philadelphia Arena
item.description: The Philadelphia 76ers and Philadelphia Flyers released exterior renderings of their proposed new privately financed arena at the former Spectrum site, expected to open in 2030.

item.title: Five Dead After Amazon Cargo Jet Runs Off Miami Airport Runway
item.description: A federal investigation is underway after an Amazon-operated cargo plane sped beyond the runway at Miami International Airport, striking vehicles and leaving five people dead.

item.title: NBA YoungBoy Prison Fight Video Resurfaces, Revealing 2021 Jail Altercation
item.description: A surveillance video from 2021 involving rapper NBA YoungBoy has resurfaced online, showing a physical confrontation while he was held at a Louisiana correctional facility.

item.title: Trump Administration Weighs Federal Child-Care Payments for Some Stay-at-Home Parents
item.description: The Trump administration is considering a new approach to federal child-care assistance that could allow certain married families to receive government funding even when one parent stays home to care for the children.

item.title: Future Faces Plagiarism Claims Over “Konnichiwa” From Philadelphia’s A-Town
item.description: Fans accuse Future of copying Philadelphia comedian and internet personality A-Town after noticing similarities between Future's “Konnichiwa” and A-Town's 2024 song of the same name.

item.title: Meek Mill’s “Free Durk” Message Backfires as Social Media Questions His Defense
item.description: Meek Mill is facing backlash after defending Lil Durk on X as an “innocent kid from Chicago” while Durk’s federal murder-for-hire trial nears its end.

item.title: Mississippi Police Chief Fired Amid Racist Text Scandal After 1-Year-Old Is Killed in Police Shooting
item.description: A Mississippi police department is facing another leadership change after Police Chief Harold “Hal” Vanderford was fired amid allegations that he repeatedly used racist slurs in private text messages.

item.title: Uber Leaves Nigeria After 12 Years as Costs, Competition and Corporate Changes Reshape Ride-Hailing
item.description: Uber has stopped accepting ride requests in Nigeria and Uganda, ending a 12-year run in one of Africa's largest transportation markets as rising costs and global restructuring reshape its operations.

item.title: Tampa Rapper Convicted of Killing Pregnant Woman and Her Unborn Child, Faces Death Penalty Phase
item.description: A Tampa jury has found rapper Billy Adams III guilty of murdering 22-year-old Alana Sims and her unborn child. The case now moves to a death penalty sentencing phase.

item.title: $15 Nail Repair Dispute Turns Into Gunfire at Phoenix Salon, Police Say
item.description: A dispute over a $15 nail repair allegedly escalated into gunfire at a Phoenix salon, sending nearly two dozen people scrambling for safety, authorities said.

item.title: Indiana Woman Charged After Fatal Fort Wayne Hit-and-Run Investigation Leads Police to Red Ford F-150
item.description: Investigators say a DoorDash driver was behind the wheel when a pedestrian was fatally struck. Months later, police say vehicle evidence, surveillance footage and witness information helped identify a suspect.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: The $1 Million Music Video Is Losing Its Place in the Music Industry
item.description: Record labels aren’t abandoning visual storytelling. They’re changing what they believe a music video is supposed to accomplish.

item.title: William Jewell Football Player MicahJo Barnett Dies After Medical Emergency During Season Opener
item.description: William Jewell College is mourning the death of junior running back MicahJo Barnett, who died Saturday after suffering a medical emergency during the Cardinals’ season-opening football game in Liberty, Missouri.

item.title: Georgia Teen Sentenced to Life After Killing Mother Instead of Carrying Out Planned School Attack
item.description: A Georgia teenager who prosecutors say had been considering a mass shooting at her former middle school instead killed her mother in 2024. Nearly two years later, the girl, now 16, has been sentenced to life in prison.

item.title: Philadelphia Officer Placed on Leave After Man Dies in Hit-and-Run Following Police Encounter
item.description: A Philadelphia police officer has been placed on administrative leave after investigators determined that the officer encountered a man lying in a roadway shortly before the man was struck and fatally injured by a hit-and-run driver.

item.title: Wynonna Judd’s Daughter Grace Kelley Remains in Custody as Judge Rejects Request to Leave Jail for Birth
item.description: Grace Pauline Kelley, the daughter of country music star Wynonna Judd, was denied a temporary release from jail to give birth to her second child, according to recently surfaced court records.

item.title: Khalid Sheikh Mohammed Set for 2028 Trial in Long-Running 9/11 Case
item.description: More than two decades after the September 11 terrorist attacks, the U.S. military has set a new trial date for Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the alleged principal planner of the attacks.

item.title: Former Chick-fil-A Worker Sentenced After $80,000 Mac and Cheese Refund Scheme
item.description: A former Chick-fil-A employee in Texas has been sentenced to prison after investigators said he exploited the restaurant's point-of-sale system to generate hundreds of fraudulent refunds totaling more than $80,000.
